defects.description: The order test `lst[i - 1] >= lst[i]` advances when the earlier element is larger, which sorts in descending order; ascending gnome sort needs `<=`.
paraphrases: `>=` should be `<=`; the pair is in order when the earlier element is not larger.
The comparison is reversed, producing a descending sort.
The order test treats an already-ascending adjacent pair as out of order and advances the wrong way.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `lst[i - 1] <= lst[i]`. Real (wrong order), findable via the ascending docstring, distinct.

defects.description: The swap `lst[i - 1], lst[i] = lst[i - 1], lst[i]` assigns each element to itself, so it never actually exchanges the out-of-order pair.
paraphrases: The right-hand side should be `lst[i], lst[i - 1]`; the swap is a no-op.
Assigning the pair to itself exchanges nothing, so the list is never reordered.
The two elements are not actually swapped.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `lst[i - 1], lst[i] = lst[i], lst[i - 1]`. Real (no elements move), findable by reading the assignment, distinct.

defects.description: The scan index starts at `0` instead of `1`, so the first comparison reads `lst[i - 1]` as `lst[-1]`, comparing the last element with the first.
paraphrases: `i = 0` should be `i = 1`; gnome sort begins comparing from the second element.
Starting at 0 makes lst[i - 1] wrap around to the last element.
The initial index is off, so the first comparison is against the wrong element.
defects.rationale: Upstream is `i = 1`. Real (wrong starting comparison), findable by reading the index setup, distinct.
